q: In Stokes' law, the constant velocity of fall is called the _____ velocity.
e: In Stokes' law, the constant velocity of fall is called the terminal velocity. Stokes' law gives the viscous drag on a small sphere as F = 6πηrv. initial or average is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: At a constant velocity of fall (terminal velocity), the upward and downward forces are in _____.
e: At a constant velocity of fall (terminal velocity), the upward and downward forces are in balance. opposition or motion is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In Newton's law of viscosity, the proportionality constant is the coefficient of _____.
e: In Newton's law of viscosity, the proportionality constant is the coefficient of viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). adhesion or capillarity is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Surface tension is the tendency of the surface of a liquid to behave like a stretched elastic _____.
e: Surface tension is the tendency of the surface of a liquid to behave like a stretched elastic skin. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l. solid or gas is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Surface tension is due to the attractive forces between liquid molecules called _____.
e: Surface tension is due to the attractive forces between liquid molecules called cohesion. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l. adhesion or friction is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of the _____ substance.
e: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of the same substance. different or opposite is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Adhesion refers to forces between molecules of _____ substances.
e: Adhesion refers to forces between molecules of different substances. same or similar is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Surface tension is the reason a _____ is able to stride along the water surface without sinking.
e: Surface tension is the reason a water strider is able to stride along the water surface without sinking. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l. stone or coin is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Paperclips, razor blades and light coins are able to rest on water without sinking although their _____ is higher than that of water.
e: Paperclips, razor blades and light coins are able to rest on water without sinking although their density is higher than that of water. viscosity or volume is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Capillary action is defined as the spontaneous flow of a liquid into a narrow tube or _____ material.
e: Capillary action is defined as the spontaneous flow of a liquid into a narrow tube or porous material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. solid or metallic is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Capillary action is caused by the combination of cohesive forces of the liquid and the _____ forces between the liquid and tube material.
e: Capillary action is caused by the combination of cohesive forces of the liquid and the adhesive forces between the liquid and tube material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. repulsive or gravitational is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In order for wicking to occur, a tube needs to be sufficiently _____ in diameter.
e: In order for wicking to occur, a tube needs to be sufficiently small in diameter. large or wide is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The rise of water underneath the ground is an example of _____ action.
e: The rise of water underneath the ground is an example of capillary action. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. viscous or turbulent is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Water is a liquid that _____ glass capillary tubes.
e: Water is a liquid that wets glass capillary tubes. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. repels or ignores is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Mercury is a liquid that does not wet glass capillary tubes, so capillarity does not occur for _____ liquids.
e: Mercury is a liquid that does not wet glass capillary tubes, so capillarity does not occur for non-wetting liquids. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. wetting or ideal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: When a glass tube is dipped into water, the _____ force between glass and water is greater than the cohesive force.
e: When a glass tube is dipped into water, the adhesive force between glass and water is greater than the cohesive force. gravitational or inertial is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Water level rises in a capillary tube until there is a sufficient mass of liquid for _____ forces to overcome the intermolecular forces.
e: Water level rises in a capillary tube until there is a sufficient mass of liquid for gravitational forces to overcome the intermolecular forces. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. electromagnetic or nuclear is a different idea, so those options are wrong.
